content: 1. Injectable contraceptives, whether for initiation or continuation, are recommended to be administered by individuals themselves, community health workers, pharmacy workers, pharmacists, traditional and complementary medicine professionals, auxiliary nurses/ANMs, nurses, midwives, associate/advanced associate clinicians, generalist medical practitioners, and specialist medical practitioners. 2. For tubal ligation procedures: It is recommended that associate/advanced associate clinicians, generalist medical practitioners, and specialist medical practitioners perform the procedure. It is suggested that nurses and midwives may also perform tubal ligation. 3. Telemedicine is recommended as an alternative to in-person interactions with healthcare workers for delivering medical abortion services, either partially or entirely. This includes assessing eligibility for medical abortion, providing counseling and instructions related to the abortion process, facilitating the administration of medications, and offering follow-up post-abortion care. However, simple informational text messages were not included in the evidence review for this recommendation. 4. There is no single recommended approach to providing abortion services. The choice of healthcare worker(s) or self-management, as well as the location of service provision, should depend on the values and preferences of the individual seeking care, available resources, and the national and local context. Multiple service-delivery approaches can coexist within a given context. 5. Scientifically accurate and understandable information at all stages. Backup referral support if needed or desired. Linkages to appropriate contraceptive services for those seeking post-abortion contraception. 6. For medical abortion at less than 12 weeks of pregnancy (using mifepristone plus misoprostol or misoprostol alone), self-management of the process is recommended. This includes: Self-assessment of eligibility (determining pregnancy duration and ruling out contraindications). Self-administration of abortion medications outside a healthcare facility without direct supervision by a trained health worker. Self-assessment of the success of the abortion. Remarks: Evidence is stronger for self-management of medical abortion for pregnancies under 10 weeks of gestation. This recommendation applies to the mifepristone plus misoprostol regimen and the use of misoprostol alone. Studies on the letrozole plus misoprostol regimen were not included in the evidence review. Regulatory frameworks may need to be adjusted to allow for self-management of medical abortion, including prescribing and dispensing authority for abortion medications. 7. For post-abortion contraception: Self-administration of injectable contraceptives is recommended. This involves the use of a syringe for intramuscular or subcutaneous injection. Compact pre-filled auto-disable devices have been developed to facilitate self-administration. 8. Over-the-counter oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) should be made available without a prescription for individuals who wish to use them. 9. Over-the-counter emergency contraceptive pills should also be made available without a prescription for individuals seeking emergency contraception. 10. The consistent and correct use of male and female condoms is highly effective in preventing the sexual transmission of HIV, reducing the risk of HIV transmission in serodiscordant couples, lowering the risk of acquiring other sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and associated conditions (such as genital warts and cervical cancer), and preventing unintended pregnancies.
